answer.description: The answer for the user. For LIMITATION, what can reliably be said. Empty string for CLARIFICATION.

assumptions.description: Reasonable non-material assumptions made to answer.

clarification_question.description: One focused question when response_type is CLARIFICATION; otherwise null.

facts.description: The facts this answer settled that later turns should reuse instead of working them out again: a list of entities, an event date with what the date means (ANNOUNCEMENT, IMPLEMENTATION_CLOSE: the trading close the change takes effect at, EFFECTIVE: the first day it applies), a period, or a definition you used. subject names what it is about (for example the index review); sources are the value references the fact rests on (out.oN..., fact.N, reference.rN, web.wN); a fact without a source is recorded as your own reading. Empty when the answer settled none or the data record already lists it unchanged.

limitations.description: Limitations of the answer, including unavailable capabilities.

memo_note.description: A note for your own later runs of this conversation, never shown to the user: what you concluded and why, what failed and why, your choices and what is still open; null for a CLARIFICATION.

methodology.description: For an ANSWER or LIMITATION that rests on an analysis: how it was reached, in plain words (the data in words rather than table or column names, the period used, filters and exclusions, the calculation steps, statistical methods and their parameters). Otherwise null.

needs_computation.description: Only in a turn whose application note says nothing is computed in it: when the request needs data or a calculation this turn cannot do, one short sentence of what must be computed. The system then hands the same message to an analysis step at once, so do not offer it in prose. Null in every other case.

label.description: The offer in a few words, in the user's language.

message.description: The request that runs when the user accepts, written as the user would ask it, complete on its own (subject, period, scope, format).

offered_action.description: The one next step this answer offers the user, when it offers one; a short yes from the user (ya, ok, gas, jalan) runs its message. Null when the answer offers nothing. A research plan is offered as a plan, not here.

angle_id.description: The approved angle's angle_id. Limits: at most 40 characters.

interpretation.description: The model's own reading of one angle; the status and the evidence are written by the backend.

answer.description: The direct answer to the angle's question, in words that match its backend status. Limits: at most 2000 characters.

follow_up.description: The most informative next step; never a buy or sell recommendation. Limits: at most 2000 characters.

usefulness.description: Why it matters for the user's decision, sized in practical terms. Limits: at most 2000 characters.

hypothesis_id.description: The approved experiment's hypothesis_id. Limits: at most 40 characters.

interpretation.description: The model's reading of one experiment (research findings v1); the verdict itself is the backend's.

answer.description: The direct answer to the user's question, in words that match the verdict. Limits: at most 2000 characters.

evidence.description: What the numbers say: effect size against the baseline, how often the outcome happened against its base rate, and how certain (how far the sample can be trusted, in words; uncertainty; smallest detectable effect). Limits: at most 3000 characters.

follow_up.description: The most informative next step; never a buy or sell recommendation. Limits: at most 2000 characters.

usefulness.description: Why it matters for the user's decision, sized in practical terms. Limits: at most 2000 characters.

verdict.description: Copied unchanged from the completed analysis's research_findings.

research_findings.description: For an ANSWER that rests on completed research: one entry per approved angle of a multi-angle run, or one per experiment of a hypothesis plan; otherwise null.

angles.description: Two to six distinct angles. Limits: 1 to 6 items.

angle_id.description: Lower-case id, unique in the plan, e.g. angle_one. Limits: matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$.

angle_question.description: The exact analytical question of this angle, unique in the plan. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

baseline_or_comparator.description: What the outcome is compared with, in words. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

candidate_count.description: Thresholds, lags, lengths or conditions evaluated inside this angle. Limits: from 1 to 50.

condition.description: The condition, signal or grouping in words. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

expected_direction.description: HIGHER or LOWER when the hypothesis expects the outcome above or below the comparator; DIFFERENT when it names no direction.

holdout_required.description: True when the latest range is kept as a holdout.

min_effect.description: The smallest effect worth knowing, as the user wrote it, only when the user named one; else null. Limits: from 0 to 1000000000.

min_effect_unit.description: P26: the unit of min_effect as the user wrote it (PERCENT, DECIMAL or BASIS_POINT); the backend converts it to the outcome's unit. Null means the outcome's unit.

multiple_testing_policy.description: NONE only for a single comparison.

outcome.description: The outcome measured, in words. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

outcome_horizon_periods.description: Analysis periods one outcome spans. Limits: from 1 to 260.

parameters.description: Every field is present; null when the angle's method does not use it.

baseline_mode.description: conditional_distribution / threshold_sensitivity: compare with the rows without the condition (COMPLEMENT) or with every row (ALL).

buckets.description: quantile_ranking: the number of equal-count buckets.

comparison.description: regime_comparison / cohort_comparison: which differences are tested.

groups.description: regime_comparison / cohort_comparison: the group labels, in the order the hypothesis reads (differences are earlier minus later).

lags.description: lead_lag: the lags tested, in analysis periods.

primary_lag.description: lead_lag: the predeclared lag (one of lags); correlation_dependency: the lag of the main correlation (null for none).

rolling_window.description: correlation_dependency: the rolling window in periods, or null.

why_distinct.description: Why this question differs from the other angles. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

items.description:
2d (user decision 2026-10-02): a released table of this conversation the research builds on, so it is part of
what the user approves; a research session loads only the tables its plan names.

output_ref.description: The table's ref from the data record, e.g. out.o3. Limits: matching ^out\.o[0-9]{1,4}$.

purpose.description: What the research takes from it, in plain words. Limits: at most 300 characters.

carried_inputs.description: Released tables of this conversation the research builds on; null for none. Limits: at most 8 items.

root_hypothesis.description: The one hypothesis every angle examines. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

analysis_frequency.description: e.g. daily; null when not relevant. Limits: at most 100 characters.

items.description:
2d (user decision 2026-10-02): a released table of this conversation the research builds on, so it is part of
what the user approves; a research session loads only the tables its plan names.

output_ref.description: The table's ref from the data record, e.g. out.o3. Limits: matching ^out\.o[0-9]{1,4}$.

purpose.description: What the research takes from it, in plain words. Limits: at most 300 characters.

carried_inputs.description: Released tables of this conversation the research builds on; null for none. Limits: at most 8 items.

confirmation_question.description: Asks the user to approve, revise or cancel the plan. Limits: at most 500 characters.

experiments.description: 1-4 experiments, one hypothesis each. Limits: 1 to 4 items.

items.description:
An experiment with the values the backend needs to judge the sample and the verdict (research findings v1,
AI_ENABLE_RESEARCH_FINDINGS). Descriptions carry no digits: the plan form is part of the system prompt.

baseline.description: What the outcome is compared with. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

candidate_count.description: Conditions, lags or parameter combinations evaluated (1-50). Limits: from 1 to 50.

condition.description: The condition or event, in plain words. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

expected_direction.description: HIGHER or LOWER when the hypothesis expects the outcome after the condition to be above or below the baseline; DIFFERENT when it names no direction.

experiment_id.description: Lower-case id, unique in the plan, e.g. experiment_1. Limits: matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$.

holdout_required.description: True when a later time range is kept out of fitting.

hypothesis.description: The hypothesis to test, in plain words. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

hypothesis_id.description: Lower-case id, unique in the plan; research_governance of the data need uses exactly this id. Limits: matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$.

min_effect.description: The smallest effect worth knowing, as the user wrote it, only when the user named one; otherwise null (the backend then uses a round-trip trading cost for returns). Limits: from 0 to 1000000000.

min_effect_unit.description: P26: the unit of min_effect as the user wrote it (PERCENT, DECIMAL or BASIS_POINT; a percentage point is PERCENT); the backend converts it to the outcome's unit. Null means the outcome's unit.

minimum_sample_unit.description: Unit of the minimum sample; null exactly when the value is null.

minimum_sample_value.description: Minimum sample size, or null for none. Limits: from 1 to 10000000.

multiple_testing_policy.description: NONE only for a single comparison.

objective.description: What this experiment establishes. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

outcome.description: The outcome measured after the condition. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

outcome_horizon_periods.description: How many analysis periods one outcome spans (a forward return over five trading days spans five); outcomes closer together than this overlap. Limits: from 1 to 260.

outcome_unit.description: PERCENT for returns in percent, DECIMAL for returns as fractions, OTHER for anything else.

success_definition.description: When one outcome counts as a success for the event-lookback share, in plain words, for example: the forward return is above zero. Limits: at most 500 characters.

anyOf.description:
M28 (golden g6 2026-10-02): when one outcome is a success, as a number the engine applies (outcome <operator>
value, in the outcome's unit), not only a sentence.

operator.description: How the outcome is compared with value.

unit.description: P26: the unit of value as the user wrote it (PERCENT for a percent, DECIMAL for a fraction, BASIS_POINT for basis points); the backend converts it to the outcome's unit. Null means the outcome's unit.

value.description: The threshold as the user wrote it. Limits: from -1000000000 to 1000000000.

success_rule.description: The success threshold as a number when the user named one (for example rises at least three percent: operator >= and value three, in the outcome's unit); the engine applies it and the answer reports the rule it used. Null when the user named none (success is then above zero). A change the user asks for later is a revised plan.

objective.description: The research objective in plain words. Limits: at most 1000 characters.

original_question.description: The user's question. Limits: at most 4000 characters.

time_scope.description: The period studied. Limits: at most 500 characters.

universe.description: Which entities, conceptually (no table names needed). Limits: at most 1000 characters.

research_plan.description: The Research Plan for RESEARCH_PLAN_CONFIRMATION (answer renders it for the user); otherwise null.

response_type.description: ANSWER when the request is answered; CLARIFICATION when a material ambiguity prevents a reliable answer; RESEARCH_PLAN_CONFIRMATION when a research question needs the user's approval of a Research Plan before any data is used; LIMITATION when a required capability is unavailable.
